about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Nothing new on US or Brazil supply this morning; Dec has slipped back under the 77.05 support into first-notice week, so old-crop Dec/Mar spread and certificate flow drive price, and high-grade certs remain a delivery risk for Dec longs rather than a comfort.
events: Dec ~76.95 (-0.37), below 77.05 support; low 76.84 (ICE via TradingView)
Crude slides again on surplus talk and inventory builds, a soft lead for polyester (Dow Jones, OilPrice.com)
Real still under pressure from fiscal worries (Bloomberg)

sugar.fundamental: Brazil first: no fresh Centre-South crush figures; crude's further slide on surplus expectations trims ethanol parity, and the weak real keeps mills hedging. Mar is holding just under the 18.02 support, so the fund buy trigger at 18.15 is not in play.
events: Oil lower on surplus expectations and US stock builds, eroding ethanol parity (Dow Jones, OilPrice.com)
BRL weakness keeps producer selling attractive (Bloomberg)

coffee.fundamental: No new supply news: the morning drop to ~280 is a price move, not a change in deliverable supply. ICE certified arabica stocks at a 1999 low and Brazil deliverability still argue for a tight nearby; watch whether Antwerp/European stocks move and the Dec/Mar inverse holds.
events: Dec ~280.2 (-6.4), back under 283.50 after failing at 284.65 (ICE via TradingView)
ICE certified arabica stocks at the lowest since 1999 (Barchart, ADMIS)
Brazil forced-labour scrutiny of Nestle suppliers keeps import-ban risk in view (Reuters)

cocoa.fundamental: Cocoa is down about 3% as climbing ICE certified stocks and talk of ample supply outweigh the slow Ivory Coast port arrivals; nothing new from Ghana's COCOBOD or on mid-crop weather this morning. No new ICCO quarterly bulletin yet (due end-November).
events: Mar ~5,024 (-153), low 5,011, nearing 4,978 support (ICE via TradingView)
Heavy rains still slowing bean transport to Ivory Coast ports (Barchart)
